description: Two sine drums tuned a fourth apart, each with a ringing tone hit and a muted slap hit, in the manner of the 808 congas and bongos

params.text: Sets the pitch of both drums: at Conga the high one runs 196Hz to 396Hz and at Bongo 400Hz to 900Hz, with the low one three quarters of that; the manual quotes half these figures
Sets how fast both tone hits fade: 40ms to 120ms at Conga and 15ms to 40ms at Bongo; the manual gives 80ms and 25ms as the two tops
Conga gives the lower pitch range and the longer decay, Bongo the higher range and the shorter one; a new module comes up at Conga
Strikes the high drum with a ringing tone, restarting its sine from zero phase
Strikes the high drum with a slap: it cuts off any tone ringing on that drum and plays a hit twice as loud that fades in 10ms
Strikes the low drum with a ringing tone, restarting its sine from zero phase
Strikes the low drum with a slap: it cuts off any tone ringing on that drum and plays a hit twice as loud that fades in 10ms

inputs.text: A rising edge above 0.5V slaps the low drum; the length of the gate makes no difference
A rising edge above 0.5V slaps the high drum; the length of the gate makes no difference
A rising edge above 0.5V plays the low drum's tone hit; the length of the gate makes no difference
A rising edge above 0.5V plays the high drum's tone hit; the length of the gate makes no difference

outputs.text: The low drum, tone and slap together, up to 5V peak
The high drum, tone and slap together, up to 5V peak

notes: a CV input is bipolar and is added to its knob: 10V there is worth the knob's whole travel, -10V cancels a knob that is fully up, and the total is clamped to the knob's own range
the slap decay is fixed at 10ms and the DECAY knob does not reach it
the two drums share one pitch setting; the low one always runs three quarters of the high one's frequency, a fourth below it
